question: Which questions below that a job applicant should prepare to ask during an interview?
options: Please describe the normal routine of this position in a typical day?
How can I gain promotion?
When do you expect to make a hiring decision as it is said in the recruitment advertisement that this position is in urgent need?
How much is the salary?
correct: Please describe the normal routine of this position in a typical day?

question: Which situation below is considered social loafing?
options: A single student works alone on a paper
A student does all the group homework
Three students work on homework together
The whole group equally work hard on group assignment
correct: A student does all the group homework

question: Which traits are taking on increasing importance in the business world today?
options: Multiculturalism and cultural intelligence
Verbal and nonverbal communication
Cultural intelligence and language
Style, pace, language and nonverbal communication
correct: Multiculturalism and cultural intelligence

question: Which implication does Self-Evaluation Maintenance (SEM) Model suggest?
options: People are more likely to compare with friends or co-workers than they are to industry or national averages.
Average students have a higher academic self-concept when attending a below-average school.
Managers may prefer sub-optimal candidates who aren't likely to challenge their standing in the organization.
Unskilled people often think they are on par or superior to their peers in tasks such as test-taking abilities.
correct: Managers may prefer sub-optimal candidates who aren't likely to challenge their standing in the organization.

question: Which strategy of evaluating information with critical thinking requires you to ask and answer such logic questions as "What question are we trying to answer?", "What point of view is being expressed?" and "What are the implications?"?
options: Read for understanding by using text coding
Examine arguments
Clarify thinking
Cultivate "habits of mind"
correct: Clarify thinking

question: When developing an application letter, which of the following should not be added in the opening of the letter?
options: The name of your referee who introduced this job to you
Your knowledge about the position or the company
Reasons why you find this position interesting
Your most significant accomplishments
correct: Your most significant accomplishments

question: When evaluating your career plan, what should you do first?
options: Looking for a career
Perform a self-assessment
Always review and revise your plan
Focus on developing goals
correct: Perform a self-assessment

question: When should we build teams?
options: A broad range of competences and different skills are required.
Minimum discretion is required.
Members' interests are different or in conflict.
An organization credits individuals for operational outputs.
correct: A broad range of competences and different skills are required.

question: When conducting a meeting, you should
options: Be bold and honest, not afraid to hurt people's feeling
Get every team member to voice out their feeling and opinions
Make it as short as possible because time is gold
Favor relationships
correct: Get every team member to voice out their feeling and opinions

question: When writing your cover letter, you should:
options: Simply copy and paste the same letter over and over.
Create an original letter for each job application.
Copy and paste the first and last paragraphs, but tailor the rest to the employer.
Establish a candidate's qualifications for a position in order to eliminate the competition.
correct: Create an original letter for each job application.

question: When analyzing your qualifications and job preferences, you will look into your most positive including
options: your achievements, background, soft skills, professional referees
your strengths, weaknesses, interests, skills
your accomplishments, education, experience, and personal traits
your awards, education, qualifications, hobbies
correct: your accomplishments, education, experience, and personal traits

question: When analyzing job preferences, which of the following questions is not necessary to consider?
options: Do you like working indoors, outside an office environment, or in varied work environments?
Do you want to work in a large company with a structured work environment, or do you prefer a small or less-structured company?
Do you want to work alone, working with other people or being in charge?
Do you want to work in a comfortable and open environment with people who share the same hobbies and personal life with you?
correct: Do you want to work in a comfortable and open environment with people who share the same hobbies and personal life with you?

question: When do the conflicts of misperceived differences arise?
options: Reinforcing or weakening each other's impact
Interpret each other's actions or emotions erroneously
Differ over how to reach goals or pursue values
Hold totally different values or rank the same values in a significantly different order
correct: Interpret each other's actions or emotions erroneously

question: When does a person obtain the expert power?
options: Person A has higher status than person B
Person A has more expertise knowledge than person B
Person A group is bigger than person B
Person A has more friend than person B
correct: Person A has more expertise knowledge than person B

question: How do critical thinking and creative thinking complement each other in a university team project?
options: They compete for dominance, hindering the team's progress.
Critical thinking accompanying creative thinking fosters fresh perspectives to look at problems and situations.
Creative thinking solely focuses on intuition, while critical thinking emphasizes logical analysis.
Critical and creative thinking are separate and don't contribute to each other in a team context.
correct: Critical thinking accompanying creative thinking fosters fresh perspectives to look at problems and situations.

question: How can develop your creative thinking skill through "Drawing"?
options: Develop ideas and expand their possibilities
Use mind-mapping to capture ideas
Explain how your ideas move beyond the status quo and contribute to a discussion
Take notes
correct: Use mind-mapping to capture ideas

question: How does a leader effectively demonstrate inspirational influence within a team?
options: By strictly enforcing rules and regulations.
By using social or interpersonal influence.
By micromanaging team members to ensure task completion.
By relying solely on positional authority to make decisions.
correct: By using social or interpersonal influence.

question: How should you respond when someone "invades" your personal space during a conversation? The question has more than one answer
options: Step back to re-establish your personal boundary
Cross your arms to block them out
Ignore the situation completely
Keep silence
correct: Step back to re-establish your personal boundary

question: Why is it important to use a good format for effective business e-mails, particularly in a professional setting?
options: Create competent impression.
Support for communicating effectively.
Reflect professionalism and follow the rules of netiquette.
All above.
correct: All above.

question: Why being socially connected is an important way of dealing with stress?
options: Because it's easy to isolate yourself when you feel stressed
Because it helps you to maintain a normal routine
Because other people can give you good advices about your problems
Because it can help distract you from your problems for a while
correct: Because other people can give you good advices about your problems

question: Why is putting yourself in nerve-racking situations can sometimes stimulate your creative thinking?
options: Certain amounts of pressure are important to keep a creative task moving forward.
When we feel stressed, it enhance our mental capacity.
Fear and frustration can trigger a sense of responsibility.
Time constraints make the task more exciting.
correct: Certain amounts of pressure are important to keep a creative task moving forward.

question: A person with individualistic orientation tends to ...
options: bring about positive outcomes to others
show their preferences when dividing resources between themselves and others
find opportunities to undermine others to get ahead
show less concerns about the outcomes of others
correct: show less concerns about the outcomes of others

question: A team is called contract team if
options: Team members have other duties to perform in their normal functional units
Team retains their responsibility for both their daily work and project work
Team members report to different managers
Team is brought in from outside in order to do project work
correct: Team is brought in from outside in order to do project work

question: Among the tips for creative thinking, what does "Sensing" mean?
options: Be a good observer of people, nature, and events around you
Be empathetic with other people
Have more fun learning
Be open to insight as ideas pop into your mind
correct: Be a good observer of people, nature, and events around you

question: An interviewer may intentionally challenge you by asking difficult questions to ...
options: see how you handle different situations
see you panic
show you the working environment can be stressful
avoid being friendly
correct: see how you handle different situations
